When preparing this album, Hua Chenyu’s original thought was to call it Size 40, since this is his own shoe size. The idea behind Size 40 was that a person really doesn’t need to take up too much space in the world. After all, you only have two feet, so you only need so much space to stand in. In true Hua Hua fashion, his sentiment is to just “go with the flow”; otherwise, there’s no need to make a big fuss. As long as you’re standing, your existence is valuable. Later, after receiving the lyrics for the song “Quasimodo’s Gift”, he changed his mind. He really liked the lyrics to the song, as they were true to the melody. This was the feeling he wanted for the album, so he decided to use the name of the song as the name of the album. He hoped everyone would learn to accept the negative things in life, even the ugliness we may encounter. Since everything has two sides, beauty may be hidden within those negative things. It’s just a matter of learning to see both the good and the bad.
Among the ten songs on the album, three were Hua’s original compositions; “Why Nobody Fights”, “Let You Go”, and “Quasimodo’s Gift”. In addition to composing for this album, Hua also participated in the entire production of the album as well as selected the other seven songs from nearly 20,000 demos. All the songs chosen for this album are connected by the themes of thunder, rain, smoke, dew, light and dreams. The album was produced by Bernard Zheng and production lasted for nine months. Zheng arranged nine of the songs in rock and roll style and he also did the piano and guitar arrangements for the album. The copywriting for Hua Chenyu’s first album was prepared by Wu Mengzhi, now a director for Hunan TV.

entry.title: Biography
entry.content:
Hua Chenyu, a male singer and songwriter from the People’s Republic of China, who also works as an arranger. He graduated from Wuhan Conservatory of Music. Hua’s main nickname in the media is “Hua hua (花花)”, which means flower.

In September 2018, five years after his debut, Hua held a two-day personal concert at China’s largest stadium, the Beijing National Stadium (Bird’s Nest), becoming the first to do so among the singers born after 1990.

Since 2021, Hua Chenyu has upgraded his personal concerts to outdoor rock festivals, each time builting a huge venue. The concert includes matinee and evening Show every day, as well as art installation and food street, attracting tens of thousands of spectators who dress up in flashy costumes and cosplay every day. They can enjoy a music carnival from afternoon to late night.

On May 4, 2024, from 3 to 6 am, Hua Chenyu held the world’s first “Sunrise Concert“ with more than 100,000 spectators.

Hua Chenyu

  • Traditional Chinese: 華晨宇
  • Simplified Chinese: 华晨宇
  • Hanyu Pinyin: Huà Chén yŭ
  • Place of Birth: Shiyan, Hubei Province, China
  • Birth: February 7, 1990
  • Child: One daughter

Biography

  • Born on February 7, 1990, in Shiyan, Hubei Province, People’s Republic of China.

  • Hua repeated his senior year of high school, and in 2010, he was admitted to his dream university - Wuhan Conservatory of Music, with the top score.

  • In 2013, Hua debuted as the Champion of “Superboy 2013“, a musical talent competition which aims at uncovering talented tomorrow new male stars.

  • In January 2014, Hua performed on the stage of The 2013 CCTV Spring Festival Gala (中国中央电视台春节联欢晚会).

  • In September 2014, one year after his debut, Hua held a two-day personal concert with an audience of over 10,000 people at the Wukesong Arena in Beijing.

  • In September 2014, Hua released his first album “Quasimodo’s Gift (卡西莫多的礼物)“.

  • From July to August 2015, Hua held a three-day personal concert with an audience of over 10,000 people at the Shanghai Indoor Stadium. The personal concert on August 1 was broadcast in real time, recording 2.64 million online viewers.

  • In December 2015, Hua released his second album “Aliens (异类)“.

  • From July to September 2016, Hua held a three-day personal concert with an audience of over 10,000 people in Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen.

  • In December 2016, Hua won the Best Asian Artist Award at the 2016 Mnet Asian Music Awards.

  • In March 2017, Hua released his third album “H“.

  • In October 2017, Hua held a two-day personal concert with an audience of over 10,000 people at the Wukesong Arena in Beijing. The personal concert on October 14 was broadcast in real time, recording 2.64 million online viewers.

  • In September 2018, five years after his debut, Hua held a two-day personal concert at China’s largest stadium, the Beijing National Stadium (Bird’s Nest), becoming the first to do so among the singers born after 1990.

  • In November 2019, Hua held a three-day personal concert at the Wuyuan River Stadium on Hainan Island. About 80% of the audience came from outside Hainan Island. According to local reports, sales at the airport duty-free shop on the first day of the concert increased by about 67%, and the live concert had a significant economic impact on the local area.

  • On December 4, 2019, Hua released the single “I’m Here AKA I Really Want to Love This World (好想爱这个世界啊)“, broking China’s digital single sales record and music app’s purchase record.

  • On February 21, 2020, Hua premiered the single “You Have To Believe This Is Not the Last Day (你要相信这不是最后一天)“ on the China singing talent show contest “Singer 2020“ to support people who have been severely affected by COVID19. This work reflects his strong feelings towards his hometown of Hubei Province and Wuhan, where he spent time in high school and university.

  • In April 2020, Hua was declared winner (AKA King of Singers) of “Singer 2020“. At the time of the program’s broadcast, Hua became the youngest “King of Singers” in history since the program aired.

  • In May 2020, Hua released his fourth album “NEW WORLD”. (Note: the MV for one of the main songs, “Bullfight (斗牛)“, was produced by a Japanese production team, directed by Mitsunori Yokobori, and animated by Yoshiki Imazu.)

  • In 2020, Hua opened a new SNS account “Mars Space Station (火星空间站)“ and started operating his art toy brand“Masper”.

  • On January 21, 2021, rumors spread on the internet that Hua Chenyu and female singer Zhang Bichen have a 2-year-old daughter. The next day, Hua admitted that he has a daughter. Immediately afterwards, Hua’s studio commented to the media that “Hua Chenyu is currently single, and the two of them will raise their child together on the premise that they will not get married, and they will be both involved in the child’s growth process.”

  • From November 26 to December 5, 2021, Hua held a six-day personal concert at the Changying Wonderland in Haikou, and premiered one new song each day, for a total of six new songs. Hua served as the general director of this concert and built a huge venue on the lawn square of the amusement park. The concert was in the form of a music festival without seats, and included two performances each day, “Matinee (2:07pm-4:30pm)” and “Evening Show (19:30pm-22:00pm)”.

  • On September 25, 2022, Hua Chenyu held an online concert “Mars Chapter“ for the 9th anniversary of his debut, rearranged 11 songs in collaboration with a symphony orchestra and choir, and experienced orchestra conducting and acapella singing for the first time. The two-hour live broadcast exceeded 200 million online views.

  • In December 2022, Hua released his fifth album “希忘Hope“.

  • In 2023, Hua Chenyu held a live tour around China in the style of a rock festival. The theme of this tour is to take fans to the great rivers and mountains of the motherland, and Hua even promised an all-night sunrise concert. In the first half of the year, Hua has held a total of 11 live concerts in four cities: Hangzhou, Chengdu, Wuhan, and Changsha.

On May 30, 2023, Hua Chenyu was certified by the Peace Elite League (PEL) under the ID of @花傲天, and officially registered with the Hangzhou LGD Team as a youth player (Attacker). The name “傲天” describes an arrogant, conceited, and invincible character that appears in Chinese internet novels and Japanese Comic.

On September 9, 2023, Hua Chenyu once again held a two-day personal concert at the Beijing National Stadium (Bird’s Nest). The theme of this concert is a perfect report in which he looks back on the 10 years since his debut. This is Bird’s Nest’s first four-sided stage after the Olympic opening ceremony. The design and construction were also handled by the production team of the 2008 Beijing Olympic and 2022 Beijing Winter Olympic Opening and Closing Ceremonies, who are also Hua Chenyu’s fans. Naturally, Hua also set a record of 100,000 viewers for a single concert in China.

  • On May 4, 2024, Hua Chenyu finally fulfilled his promise after 3 years to hold a concert where he can watch the sunrise with his fans! The world’s first solo concert to greet the sunrise in the early morning. Fortunately, after several days of cloudy weather, everyone finally saw the sunrise! The Sunrise Concert was held from 3:00 am to 6:00 am, and more than 100,000 people greeted the sunrise while singing “Growing Toward the Sun (向阳而生)“!

  • On May 24-26, 2024, Hua Chenyu held his first personal concert outside mainland China in Hong Kong. The concert still took the form of a rock festival, and was held for three consecutive days at the Central Harbourfront Event Space, facing the Victoria Harbour.

  • NEW⇒ In January 2025, Hua released his sixth album “TIPPING POINT (量变临界点)“.

Celebrity Endorsement

On November 2, 2020, Hua Chenyu served as one of the four celebrity endorsers for “Game For Peace”.
During the next three years, other celebrity endorsements changed frequently, but Hua Chenyu was the only one who did not cancel his contract.

  • On April 26, 2021, the game’s second anniversary theme song “Flying Conductor (飞行指挥家)“ was officially released.

  • On March 13, 2022, the “Game For Peace” Peace Elite League (PEL)’s annual theme song “Iconic moment (名场面)“ was released.

  • On August 17, 2023, “Game For Peace” Peace Elite League (PEL)’s annual theme song “War God in Dire Straits (绝境战神)“ was released.

1. Achievements

  • “Mars Park-Style Concerts 2.0” continues the signature format of Matinee + Evening Show, providing a moment of non-stop revelry for fans to play all day long. Inside the amusement park, a diverse range of entertainment is offered, including integrates gaming, interactive zones, gourmet food, and various leisure activities. The stage design centers on the theme of “Eternity,” shattering the traditional single-format concert model to achieve breakthroughs in both visual presentation and content arrangement. While preserving the iconic artistic style of the Mars Concerts, it deeply integrates natural landscapes to create an exclusive stage that blends high-tech aesthetics with natural vibes, making the audience feel as if they are in a secret “Martian” realm.

  • A brand-new “Twin Setlist” is introduced. By alternately performing different setlists across the tour dates, each show is given distinct highlights. Through this multi-layered musical experience, the audience can fully appreciate the unique charm of the stage created by Hua Chenyu.

2. Anecdote

Yuxi (Cancelled)

  • The performances scheduled for May 1-2 and 4-5, 2026, which were to serve as the opening stop for “Mars Park-Style Concerts 2.0” at Fuxian Lake (the second deepest freshwater lake in China) in Yuxi, Yunnan, were abruptly cancelled due to force majeure on April 22 – just one week before the event. Dismantling of the stage facilities, which cost over 2 billion JPY and were nearly complete, began that very night.

  • According to media interviews and reports published before the cancellation, the decision to locate “Mars Park-Style Concerts 2.0” at Fuxian Lake was prompted by a warm invitation from Yuxi City. The event’s realization came only after navigating numerous challenges and setbacks.

  • According to various estimates, the losses incurred by Hua Chenyu and the organizers from stage construction costs, hundreds of thousands of ticket refunds, VIP ticket perks and merchandise for sale, and compensation for flight and hotel cancellations alone will reach billions of JPY. This does not include investments in fixed assets such as local real estate purchases, infrastructure development, environmental protection support, and the establishment of supporting facilities.

  • At the final concert last year, Hua Chenyu announced the purchase of three plots of land in Yunnan to build a physical “Mars Home”. These plots were designated for a permanent stage and audience area, lifestyle facilities like B&Bs and cafes, and the creation of a “Mars Utopia”. When the concert was cancelled, the B&B and cafe were already in operation. In particular, the B&B “Warm House” had previously selected guests (limited to concert-goers) via livestream to stay during the concert period for a special price of 3 RMB per day; all payments have now been refunded, and the offer has been changed to allow all booked guests to stay for free.

  • On the night the cancellation was announced, Hua Chenyu held a Livestream, performing several songs rearranged specifically for the concerts to comfort his fans. A few days later, at the China Blue Zuili Lake Music Festival, Hua Chenyu revealed that on the very night he learned of the cancellation, he had organized a specialized task force to scout other Chinese cities for a new venue and had already dispatched them to the field.

entry.title: Skincare Brand “重点POINZ”
entry.content:
As a co-founder, Hua Chenyu launched the skincare brand “重点POINZ”.
The brand was co-founded by Xiaokuo Group (the parent company of the oral care brand Canban, for which Hua Chenyu serves as the ambassador) and Hua himself. This signifies that Hua Chenyu is no longer merely a brand ambassador; instead, he is deeply involved in every step of the brand’s chain, from product R&D to visual identity creation, in his capacity as a co-founder.
With the core philosophy of “Smoothing out life’s little burrs”, POINZ is committed to pioneering a world of “Micro-care”, advocating a lifestyle that encourages people to “Focus on the essentials, and live a little more relaxed”.
Its debut collection covers high-frequency daily essentials, including floral water, plant essential oil bracelets, cooling lithospermum soothing balm, hand cream, and lip balm. Since then, the brand has sequentially launched household chemical products such as laundry detergent and floor cleaners.


Offline Events

March 22, 2026

To celebrate the brand’s launch, a pop-up store opened in Hangzhou. That evening, Hua Chenyu made a surprise appearance at the venue to interact with fans and conduct a live stream.
Due to the last-minute nature of the decision, Hua paired a red hat with a yellow tie found at his home to match the brand’s design style. This look was jokingly dubbed the “Trump-style outfit” among fans and became a hot topic.

» Ticket Purchase Guide «

Origin

When first debuted, Hua Chenyu was often referred to as the “boy from Mars (火星弟弟)” by the media, due to his slightly strange personality.
Hua simply made “MARS” his image symbol, and promised his fans that “someday we will return to Mars together”. To fulfill this promise, Hua named his personal concert “MARS CONCERT (火星演唱会)”.
By the way, His fans also received the nickname “ET (Martian，火星人)“.

Achievements

  • In 2021, Hua Chenyu pioneered the rock theme park-style concerts in the form of an outdoor music festival.

  • The world’s first solo concert specifically be held in the early morning to greet the sunrise.

  • Being the youngest singer to hold a personal concert at China’s largest stadium, the Beijing National Stadium (Bird’s Nest), and the only singer under the age of 30 to hold a concert there. Also being the first singer to introduce a four-sided stage to the Bird’s Nest, setting a record for a personal concert in China by attracting 100,000 people to a single performance.

  • The stage design has won the MUSE Design Awards four times. Among them, 2021’s Rock Theme Park-Style Concerts, 2023’s four-sided stage in the Bird’s Nest, and 2024’s Sunrise Concert all won the Platinum Award in 2024; and the lighting design of Mars Concert 2024’s four-sided stage won the Lighting Design of the Year in 2025.

  • Breaking records for the largest audience in a single concert at stadiums in various cities

Regular Parts of MARS CONCERT

  • Greet fans with “Welcome home (欢迎回家)” as the first greeting.

  • When performing the song “The World is a Zoo (世界是个动物园)“, Hua always sings “oiaioiaioiaiaio” with a random melody and makes his fans repeat it. The melody gradually becomes more complex, and it always ends on a high note that fans can’t sing, thus becoming a reason for Hua to laugh at his fans.

  • Before the concert ends, be sure to thank each staff and partner, such as band members, company, security team, fire brigade, etc. Every time Hua pronounces a name, ETs shout “Thank you”.

  • From 2014 to 2017, always sing Leslie Cheung’s famous song I Am What I Am (我) as the last encore. Since this is a very special song for Hua and he only has the strength to sing it once a year, he wanted to use that only opportunity for MARS CONCERT.

  • In 2018, after singing I Am What I Am (我), Hua went on to sing an unreleased new song “New World (新世界)” and declared to fans, “From now on, I will take you to a new world.” Through this action, Hua embarked on a new journey in his life.

  • Starting in 2021, MARS CONCERT has been upgraded to an outdoor rock festival. Hua put his rock songs in the more exciting Evening Show, and put his early songs and some pop songs in the more relaxed Matinee. Also, rearranging songs into unplugged version for Matinee and singing along with guest Zuo Li has become a regular occurrence.

  • We don’t know since when, fans started asking Hua for kisses during impromptu interactions, and Hua always satisfied fans with a “kiss song” after a “brewing”.

  • During the performance of “Ship of Theseus“, fans in the audience spontaneously hummed polyphonic harmonies, creating a magnificent choral effect.

  • For the song “Bizarre Psychology AKA Quirky Psychology“, band members automatically lined up behind Hua to patrol the venue, wearing hilarious masks/headpieces secretly prepared with unique themes for each show. Both the stage crew and audience eagerly anticipated Hua’s reactions—whether laughter or shock—to these surprises. Classic themes included “Calabash Brothers” (a Chinese animated series); “Teletubbies” (with Hua mimicking their tiptoe wobble and bouncing); “Plants vs. Zombies” (Hua imitating a Peashooter); Hangzhou’s “The Legend of the White Snake”; and Changsha’s “Dorky Orange (呆橘)“ series alongside petrified-with-shock memes (which Hua mistakenly thought were “Charcoal ball (黑煤球)“, leading him to affectionately pat his head).

  • Since 2023, during each tour stop after the national college entrance examination every year, Hua Chenyu has invited outstanding examinees among his fans who have been admitted to China’s top universities, as well as excellent teachers from the tour host cities, to watch the concert for free from the best seats. This initiative is named the “Mars Incentive Program”.

  • NEW⇒ May 4 is the first anniversary of the sunrise concert. 2,000 drones were launched to simulate the sun and spell out the words: “You are my sun — by Big Brother. (你们就是我的太阳 ——大哥)”, setting a record for the number of drones launched above the concert venue. (Due to the large gathering of people at the performance site, for safety reasons, the launch of such a large number of drones is usually not allowed). Since then, a large-scale fireworks show and drone show have been arranged for every Rock Theme Park-Style Concert.

  • During the second day’s performance, immediately after singing “Arrival“, the lift stage malfunctioned. With parkour-like agility, Hua leapt down multiple platform levels consecutively, igniting frenzied cheers throughout the venue.

» Fuzhou Concerts Photo Gallery «

Changsha

  • On March 22-23, Hua Chenyu returned to his debut city Changsha to hold Concerts for two consecutive days.

  • A drone conducting high-speed aerial filming around and the stage crashed at a corner of the platform, with the entire incident broadcast live on the giant screen in first-person perspective.

  • While singing the line “There is a letter, A letter for you from the future” in “Let’s Go and Watch the Sunrise“, Hua pulled out a letter from his chest. The stationery featured a simple sketch widely cherished among the fans: Hua and ET sharing a kiss at sunrise.

  • During the second day’s concert, Hua made a weather-based bet with fans, rooted in his “Little Sun” legend (believed to bring sunshine to concert dates). Despite prior continuous rain, Changsha experienced unusually scorching weather during the concerts, followed by a sudden temperature drop the next day. Hua pledged that If the next concert in Xi’an also has clear skies, fans win—and he’ll grant one collective wish.

» Changsha Concerts Photo Gallery «

Xi’an

  • April 5-6 (Qingming Festival holiday in China), Hua Chenyu held consecutive concerts in Xi’an, an ancient capital of 13 dynasties.

  • On Day 1, Hua mentioned “keeping the performance more family-friendly” as his father and sister were in the audience, while teasing a “an outfit requiring prolonged mental preparation” for Day 2. Fans speculated wildly about its boldness, only to discover a full-body leopard print ensemble the next day.

  • The most renowned historical site in Xi’an is the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor’s Terracotta Army. Staffs from a Terracotta Warriors-themed musical troupe watched the lives in Qin Shi Huang and warrior cosplay. During the performance of “Light Up the Bonfire at the Galaxy’s End“ they joined fans’ dancing in the arena pit.

  • While filming a vlog at a snack street the day before, Hua passed by a fan girl without being recognized. At the concert, Hua publicly screened the coincidentally recorded encounter, jokingly awarding her an autographed “reunions feel distant” (from “In the Morning Light, There’s You“ lyrics) certificate, and gifted her a whole set of merchandise.

  • Having lost the weather-based bet with fans (no rain occurred), Hua voluntarily proposed fulfilling the wager by dancing to choreography from his “Bizarre Psychology AKA Quirky Psychology“ MV - his first official concert dance performance. On Day 2, Hua executed the routine wearing Lop-eared rabbit shaped woolen hat, then turned completely red from shyness.



» Xi'an Concerts Photo Gallery «

Foshan

  • China celebrated Labor Day from May 1 to 5, and Hua Chenyu held three consecutive Theme Park-style Concert from May 2 to 4 in Foshan. The third day (May 4) marked the first anniversary of the sunrise concert, and Hua prepared many surprises for the Martians.

  • Hua Chenyu sent gift boxes by express delivery to audiences in the inner area (CN¥1280/980). The boxes included a small bottle of perfume, lipstick, a key-shaped ornament, and a plastic wristband.

  • Hua Chenyu has twice posted photos on social media of himself cooking fried rice. Encouraged by enthusiastic Martians, he promised to treat everyone to his “Chenyu Fried Rice.” He shared his fried rice recipe and set up “Chenyu Fried Rice” booths, offering free portions to all (each person could line up multiple times to receive a 50ml cup-sized serving). At the concert, he mentioned that a total of 3 tons of rice were consumed over the three days.

  • During the live broadcast on the day before the performance, Hua Chenyu fried rice at the stall on the spot. He originally wanted to distribute the fried rice to the fans who were watching outside the venue, but due to the large safety distance on both sides of the enclosure, he couldn’t hand it out and had to give up with regret.












  • Various facilities in the concert were upgraded, including:

    • Air-conditioned rest area in the VIP section (The large tent was enclosed with transparent plastic, allowing people to rest while still being able to watch the concert at the same time.)
    • All areas provided free drinking water, ice, and anti-heatstroke medicine.
    • Several high-end mobile toilets and changing rooms were set up, with an increased number of women’s restrooms, along with a variety of feminine products.
    • After a brief heavy rain on the second day, when the lawn became muddy, buckets and water hoses were provided for washing feet.

  • In the afternoon sessions of the concert, the usual game segment was replaced with an Airplane Chess featuring various obstacles, intentionally designed to make Hua receive “punishments.” He ended up doing many things he normally wouldn’t do, such as dancing, mimicking emojis, taking rapid selfies, and creating live drawing.



  • In keeping with local traditions, a lion dance troupe was invited to perform in the plaza on the third day.

  • On the first day of the concert, the weather was hot. On the second day, there was a brief heavy rain during the middle of the event. The game segment was skipped, and many pieces of equipment were damaged. Repairs caused a 20-minute delay to the evening session. During the rain, audiences were allowed to leave the venue to take a break, and re-entry was arranged once the rain had stopped.

  • The heavy rain didn’t dampen the fans’ enthusiasm – many of them started playing in the rain, which eased Hua’s worries about everyone. During the evening session, he mentioned that he had seen various videos online of fans having fun in the water.

  • On the third day, to celebrate the first anniversary of the sunrise concert, Hua had a custom cake made (see photo).
    Zuo Li prepared a custom banner (see photo), with the words: “This is a remarkable first anniversary of the sunrise concert!”


  • The surprise of the evening show on the third day was that 2,000 drones were launched to simulate the sun and spell out the words: “You are my sun — by Big Brother. (你们就是我的太阳 ——大哥)”. It had been kept secret from the fans all the time. The drones could only be flown when the weather was fine at night. So, since the daytime, Hua had been particularly worried. He checked the sky several times and talked about various topics related to the sky.




  • On the third day, just like during last year’s sunrise concert, over ten thousand fans who couldn’t get tickets gathered outside the venue to watch. Hua Chenyu greeted them through the big screen. During the “kiss” segment, he even asked the cameraman to come onstage and zoom in close, so that his face would appear more clearly on the big screen, making it easier for those watching from far outside the venue to see.
» Foshan Concerts Photo Gallery «

Qingdao

  • On May 17, Hua Chenyu continued his live tour in Qingdao.

  • Due to rain on the second day of the Foshan concerts, Hua won this “weather-based bet”. He proposed a fun trade-off for the Qingdao concert: he wanted to experience the same pleasure fans have—relaxing, eating, and even lying down while watching a concert! Consequently, at the following Qingdao concert, the fans performed a full sing-along of “Light Up the Bonfire at the Galaxy’s End“. This allowed Hua to relax on stage, enjoying local barbecue and beer. He even shared a toast with his band and downed a full glass of beer on the spot.



» Qingdao Concert Photo Gallery «

Chengdu

  • From May 31 to June 1, coinciding with China’s traditional Dragon Boat Festival and International Children’s Day respectively, Hua Chenyu held two consecutive concerts in Chengdu.

  • This year, the VJ for “The World is a Zoo“ features real-time rendering animation that randomly transforms the singer and audience into cartoon animal images, which is quite intriguing. For the Chengdu concerts, it was a panda-themed special edition, where everyone’s transformed image became a panda, and the background turned into a bamboo forest habitat scene.

  • During the live stream the night before the concert, Hua accepted fans’ suggestions and challenged a high ponytail hairstyle for the second day’s performance. Additionally, since Hua announced the high ponytail during the first day’s concert, fans flocked to take overnight flights to attend! Tickets sold out completely that same day. During the performance, Hua, who noticed fans’ overnight travel updates on social media, kindly reminded everyone to rest and eat properly.

  • Also during the live stream, Hua agreed to bring a camera on stage when the opportunity arises, allowing everyone to see his perspective from the stage. True to his word, after the performance, Hua released a first-person selfie video specially recorded during rehearsals, showing his entrance descending onto the stage from above.

  • The second day of the performance coincided with International Children’s Day, and Hua invited visually impaired children to the concert through a charity organization.

» Chengdu Concerts Photo Gallery «

Zhengzhou

  • On June 14, Hua Chenyu continued his live tour in Zhengzhou, Henan Province.

  • Due to rain on the first day of the Chengdu concert, Hua won the “weather-based bet” again. His prize request was an a cappella chorus performed by the entire audience. He divided the tens of thousands of fans into three vocal sections based on their seating areas and taught each group a one-measure melody. By snapping his fingers and waving his arms to conduct the rhythm while singing the lead melody himself, he led the entire stadium in a collaborative a cappella rendition of “Mayfly“.

  • Even in the subsequent “Kiss Song”, Hua divided fans into three vocal parts to chorus “mo-mo-da-“ (meaning “kiss” in Chinese).

  • Hua created a brand-new intro music for “Ship of Theseus“, and the VJ animation for this intro music incorporated the creative concept of “Luoshan Shadow Puppetry” – an intangible cultural heritage. During the interlude of the performance, Hua performed Tai Chi to the music, a symbol of Chinese culture that originated in Henan Province.

» Zhengzhou Concert Photo Gallery «

Shenyang

  • On June 28, Hua Chenyu held a concert in Shenyang, Liaoning Province, marking his first concert in China’s northeastern region. He admitted that coming to the Northeast made him want to tell jokes, even imitating famous sketches from the Spring Festival Gala on site and sharing several corny jokes.

  • This was also the last tour concert of the first half of the year, with the next one resuming on August 29 – the day of China’s Qixi Festival (also known as Chinese Valentine’s Day). This schedule was mainly to avoid the intense summer heat, which Hua referred to as the “summer break.”

  • The evening before the concert, Hua held a surprise livestream called “Martian Summer Break Class Meeting”, recounting memories from each concert of the first half of the year in turn.

  • On the day of the concert, a fan couple got married and invited online all fans to attend, then go to the concert together that night. Learning about this via social media, Hua sang “We Meet When Flowers Fade“ with the audience at the venue as a blessing to the newlyweds. He also gifted them tickets to the next concert, inviting them to spend their first Valentine’s Day (Qixi Festival) as a married couple together.

  • In the previous “weather-based bet” in Zhengzhou, it didn’t rain, so the fans won and Hua had to grant one of fans’ requests. Therefore, based on feedback seen in the live stream comments the night before, Hua accompanied the audience in chorusing “Warm House“. Since it was a last-minute decision, neither Hua nor the band had rehearsed it. There were parts where everyone sang wrong, and Hua even made mistakes while playing the piano.

» Shenyang Concert Photo Gallery «

Suzhou

  • From August 29 to 31, Hua Chenyu kicked off the second half of his live tour in Suzhou. Since August 29 (Friday) is “Qixi Festival”, which is the Chinese Valentine’s Day based on the romantic legend of the Zhinü and Niulang, Hua specially arranged a concert on this non-weekend day.

  • At the concert venue, the fences inside the stadium were elaborately decorated with 80,000 red roses, creating a dreamlike “Mars Rose Garden”. On the evening before Qixi Festival, Hua Chenyu specially held a live stream to interact with fans – he not only showed everyone the sea of roses at the venue but also took fans on a first-person view experience of the rehearsal for his aerial entrance during the opening song.

  • This year, the Qixi Festival gift Hua prepared for the on-site audience was a limited-edition puzzle featuring the Mars flower bouquet pattern. Additionally, at the pop-up store, the annual Qixi Festival-limited red butterfly pastries (butterfly-shaped puff pastries) were launched.

  • Hua Chenyu’s connection with Suzhou city dates back to several years ago, when he participated in the singing competition TV show “The Next (天籁之战)“ in Suzhou and commuted there every week. On this show, Hua fully demonstrated his songwriting ability and singing ability, and rearranged many songs that became massive hits.

  • Once again, during the stadium performance, several sophisticated rocket-shaped fireworks were set off while “Eternal Flame“ was being performed.

  • In the previous “weather-based bet” in Shenyang, Hua won again, and he shared another wish: “Actually, I have a small wish that I’ve kept hidden in my heart for more than ten years. Today, just in time for Qixi Valentine’s Day, I want to share this wish. My wish is that all Martians will be happy now and always in the future.” At the same time, Hua held up a carefully prepared “fan service board” (a board with messages for fans), which read, “Martians, strike a heart pose if you feel happy” and “How deep can love be?” Hua continued, “A few days ago, during a music festival in Qingdao, I was also singing ‘King and Beggar‘. Back then, I saw a fan – a little Martian – holding a board that said, ‘Hua Chenyu, strike a heart pose if you feel happy.’ So I struck a heart pose to her. Today, I want to say to all the Martians here: if you feel happy, can you strike a heart pose for me?” The fans responded one after another by striking heart poses.

  • On the third day, it was drizzling. While singing “Arrival“, lightning flashed in the sky, which perfectly matched the stage’s light cascade, creating a unique sense of destiny. During the intro of the most thrilling song “Madhouse“, a huge bolt of lightning also lit up the sky.

  • Hua Chenyu showed off his muscles on stage for the first time. Later, while changing clothes backstage, a colleague teased him, saying, “Bro, that was your first time showing off your muscles on stage, and it looked a bit clumsy.” This made him feel “a little shy – I originally wanted to look cool, but it turned out kind of clumsy.”

Nanjing

  • From October 4th to 6th, during China’s National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival long holiday, the rock theme park-style concerts were held for three consecutive days again after a major upgrade. Additionally, during the holidays before and after the concert (October 1st-3rd, October 7th-8th), the amusement area was open to all the public for free under the name of “Mars Utopia (火星乌托邦)”.

  • On both sides and the back of the “Planet” stage, dozens-of-meters-long elevating extended stages were newly installed.

  • As the stage design for “Ship of Theseus“, a huge inflatable wooden boat was newly placed as a real set in the center of the main stage. This inflatable boat was quickly set up and dismantled by the staff before and after the song performances.

  • Based on previous years’ climate, temperatures drop after autumn in October, so measures like ginger tea were prepared. However, this autumn encountered an unusual heatwave; Hua Chenyu suffered from heatstroke due to the sun during the matinee and thus weared an ice vest again to cool himself down. Moreover, a large number of cooling pads were purchased and provided to the audience for free.




  • The publicly open “Mars Utopia” included more games, food and beverage options, and art installations than the previous park-style concerts.









  • During the three-day concerts, a drone-coordinated fireworks show was held every day, matching the songs “Eternal Flame“, “Bullfight“, “Warm House“, “Light Up the Bonfire at the Galaxy’s End“, as well as the final songs of the matinee and the evening Show, with a different design each day. Hua Chenyu himself stated that the cost of the three-day fireworks show exceeded the value of a villa.

Haikou

  • From November 28 to 30, 2025, the Mars Concert returned to Haikou Changying Wonderland, marking a comeback to the venue of its first Rock Theme Park-Style Concert held in 2021.

  • The concert was originally scheduled to take place near Wenchang Spacecraft Launch Site in Wenchang City, Hainan Province. The aim was to allow the audience to witness the satellite launch by the modified Long March-7 carrier rocket on the evening of November 30 directly from the concert venue. However, due to various reasons, the ongoing stage construction was halted, and the concert had to change venues less than two weeks before the show. It was finally decided to be held at Haikou Changying Wonderland, which had experience hosting Rock Theme Park-Style Concert. The promotional poster also incorporates the elements of the 2021 Mars Concert poster.

  • Prior to the venue change, Haikou Changying Wonderland, the host venue, took the initiative to promise that all audiences could enter the park for free and enjoy all amusement facilities throughout December by presenting their 2021 or 2025 concert tickets.


  • The giant metal ring devices that resemble planetary orbits and surround the entire VIP area, a stage set that had accompanied the Mars Concert for a full three years, was retired after this Haikou concerts. A brand-new set will be used for the Rock Theme Park-Style Concert next year. The ring is affectionately nicknamed “环环 (Huanhuan, which means rings)” by fans, and Zuo Li specially presented Hua Chenyu with a custom plaque commemorating Huanhuan’s retirement during the Matinee on the third day.

  • Inspired by a drum beat-matching game on TikTok, Hua Chenyu set up a drum beat-matching game themed after his song “Bizarre Psychology AKA Quirky Psychology“ in the amusement park. Unfortunately, both he and his band members all failed miserably at the game. He even tried to match the beat during his Evening Show, but failed two nights in a row; instead, the action of holding his head and squatting down after failing actually hit the beat.

  • During the Evening Show on the third day, Hua Chenyu held a live streaming device and broadcast the first-person view of his aerial entrance on the large screen. This fulfilled the promise he had made to fans during a live stream before this year’s Suzhou concerts.

  • Fireworks and drone shows were still featured in Haikou concerts. The drone show on the first day was themed around Mars Concert and roses, while the second day’s theme was Hua’s beloved cat Perper. On the third day, due to the drizzling rain that Hua jokingly called “moisturizing spray”, the drones were obscured by mist and hard for the audience to see. When leaving the stage, Hua Chenyu live-streamed on the large screen and showed the originally planned drone show renderings to the audience with a phone.

  • During the Evening shows on the second and third days, Hua Chenyu took selfies with the audience’s phones at the end of the extended stage.

  • Before the Matinee on the third day, Hua Chenyu went on stage early and took a full lap of selfies with a selfie stick. He later joked that this was to test the temperature and wind speed.

  • At the end of Haikou concerts, Hua Chenyu officially announced that the 2.0 version of the Rock Theme Park-Style Concert would be launched next year, but the specific method needed to be kept confidential to prevent the idea from being plagiarized. He also shared the origin story of the 1.0 version of the concerts that started in 2021. He hopes to be regarded as just an ordinary Martian, and to eat, play, and enjoy ordinary joys with everyone in the Mars Utopia.

Nanning

  • The Mars Concert Tour’s annual cycle is calculated according to the Chinese lunar calendar. Therefore, the Nanning concert on January 2, 2026, still falls under the 2025 tour schedule. The Shenzhen concerts from February 6 to 8 will be the final concerts of Mars Concert 2025.

  • As a New Year’s gift, Hua Chenyu presented every audience with a cloth-made calendar themed around the “Charcoal ball (黑煤球)“.













  • Hua Chenyu announced that the stage art design for this four-sided stage, which has been in use for three years, will come to an end this year. Next year, brand-new stage art design will be adopted not only for the Rock Theme Park-Style Concert, but also for the four-sided stages.

Shenzhen

  • From February 6–8, 2026, Hua Chenyu held the finale of his 2025 concert tour in Shenzhen. Among these dates, February 7th was his 36th birthday, marking his first-ever public birthday celebration since his debut.

  • During the birthday concert on February 7th, fan-organized celebrations included: a collective sing-along of the “Happy Birthday” song following the “3-2-1” countdown of the “Kiss Song”; as Hua walked onto the extended stage, audience members in that section raised different colored fluorescent boards to form massive mosaic characters, while all spectators held up their own cake-shaped ornaments.



  • The concert organizers arranged several tributes, including: distributing confetti popper to every audience member, featuring customized patterns and confetti shapes; a surprise appearance by a mascot in “Charcoal ball (黑煤球)” costume to present a birthday cake after the song “For Forever“, leading the fans in a synchronized birthday chant via the giant screens; and lighting up countless golden LED strips specially draped along the edges of the stadium stands.


  • While performing the song “Conversations with Martian Children“, Hua finally couldn’t help but burst into tears, marking the first time he was too choked up to continue singing; the audience spontaneously took over, singing the entire second half of the song in a loud, powerful chorus.



  • Throughout these three concerts, Hua several times stopped singing during unannounced segments and handed the mic to the audience; every time, the fans caught the lyrics and melody perfectly, leaving him both shocked and joyful.

  • As this was the final stop of the 2025 tour, Hua announced that he had acquired three plots of land in Yunnan, which will be used to build the physical “Mars Home.”

entry.title: “Sound Trek 2025 (声鸣远扬)” - Singing Competition
entry.content:
1. About the show

Hua Chenyu has been invited to serve as a resident judge for the final stages (elimination rounds) of the singing competition “Sound Trek (声鸣远扬) 2025”. Starting from November 9, 2025, the program is broadcast live every Sunday at 7:30 PM across multiple TV stations and various apps, including YouTube.

Yin Xiumei, a national treasure-level soprano singer in China, and Na Ying, a legendary female singer who holds an unshakable top position in the Chinese music industry. Na Ying and Hua Chenyu first met through the music program “Infinity and Beyond 2023“ and have since built a profound friendship.











2. Episode Details

EP1: Battle for the Top 18 (Part 1)

November 9, 2025

  • Afternoon Media Briefing Live Stream
    In response to a question about how to devote oneself fully to every vocal performance, Hua Chenyu replied, “It requires a genuine love for the song.”

  • First Live Broadcast of the Elimination Rounds
    The three judges continuously presented the hosts with difficult challenges, leading netizens to jokingly dub them the “Demon Orb (魔丸) Mentors” (a reference to the popular Chinese animated film series “Ne Zha”). Throughout the episode, Hua remained consistently strict in checking the contestants for “off-pitch” singing.

EP2: Battle for the Top 18 (Part 2)

November 16, 2025

At the end of the episode, the judges requested an expansion of the qualification slots and won the right to save two additional contestants.
Hua chose a street musician with a passion for songwriting, whose previous elimination he had deeply regretted.

EP3: Top 18 to Top 12

November 23, 2025

The judges once again requested a rule change on-site, promoting one more contestant to the next round.

EP4: Top 12 to Top 10

November 30, 2025

Hua was absent due to his Mars Concert 2025; female singer-songwriter Laure Shang filled in as a proxy.

EP5: Top 10 to Top 8

December 7, 2025

EP6: Top 8 to Top 7

December 14, 2025

EP7: Top 7 Replacement Round (Resurrection Round)

December 21, 2025

Hua revealed for the first time why he didn’t showcase his most proficient styles or many original songs during his time on “Superboy 2013.” He explained that by the time he realized he should have meticulously envisioned his future career path, it was already too late—the competition had reached its final stages (around the Top 5 to Top 3). He shared that his first original song released after the competition, “Why Nobody Fights,” was composed in a style intended for mass sing-alongs at the Bird’s Nest (Beijing National Stadium), after he had firmly identified his path toward large-scale stadium concerts.
Consequently, Hua assigned the contestants a task: to formulate an initial blueprint for their future direction.

EP8: Top 7 to Top 6

December 28, 2025

In this episode, Hua’s scoring was extremely rigorous, based on “assignment grading” standards. He evaluated performances comprehensively from two aspects: not just the quality of the performance, but also its alignment with the contestant’s future career blueprint.
Fellow judge Yin Xiumei reversed the roles by giving Hua an “assignment,” commissioning him to create a new musical work.

EP9: Top 6 to Top 5

January 4, 2026

On New Year’s Day, Hua led the Top 6 contestants to perform at the # Hunan TV Countdown Party.
A contestant Hua had high expectations for was unexpectedly eliminated.

EP10: Top 5 to Top 4

January 11, 2026

EP11: Determining the Top 3

January 18, 2026

A contestant performed an ultra-high note. Hua sang along quietly while listening and, prompted by those around him during the critique, perfectly replicated that high-note part.

EP12: Determining the Champion

January 25, 2026

While critiquing a contestant, Hua relatably vented about the hardships of his past performances, where he was also made to sing while being hoisted up in a lying position.
Wang Meng, China’s former short-track speed skating champion known as “The Queen”, couldn’t help but go on at length while guest-commentating on a contestant’s performance, recalling the time she performed a duet with Hua on a variety show.

1. Achievements

  • After 3 years, Hua Chenyu finally fulfilled his promise to hold a concert where he can watch the sunrise with his fans! The world’s first solo concert specifically be held in the early morning to greet the sunrise. Fortunately, after several days of cloudy weather, everyone finally saw the sunrise!

  • The stage design had been significantly upgraded based on last year’s design, and the music team had also been replaced. Producer Bernard Zheng, who has collaborated with Hua since his debut, served as music director and added new arrangements to half of Hua’s songs.

  • Teachers and students from the China Academy of Art designed an installation art exhibition for the concert.

  • On June 2, a re-recording album “Sunrise Concert Speciel Album“ including 8 rearranged tracks selected from the Sunrise Concert, was released.

  • Breaking records for the largest audience in a single concert at stadiums in various cities.

  • The Sunrise Concert’s stage design won the Platinum Award at the MUSE Design Awards in 2024; and the lighting design of four-sided stage won the Lighting Design of the Year in 2025.

» Poster and Stage Design Photo Gallery «

2. Anecdote

  • For the Sunrise Concert in Yantai, tens of thousands of fans who couldn’t buy tickets gathered on the beach and lawns outside the venue all night. Organizers set up special safe viewing areas on the beach, added speakers, and even opened the entrance to let outside fans in for the final few songs before the concert ended.

  • When holding a stadium concert, Hua always rents out a shopping mall atrium in the city to open a pop-up store and sell peripheral goods and snacks.

  • A different sentence was printed each day on the long ribbon paper that was sprayed at the end of the performance. However, on the first day in Hong Kong, the spraying equipment was damaged by rain and the long ribbon paper could not be released.

Yantai Concert

  • This time, Hua’s personal concert still took the form of a rock festival, and was held for three consecutive days (in the evenings of May 1-2 and early morning of May 4) in the beautiful coastal city of Yantai in eastern China.

  • The concert on the third day was held from 3:00 am to 6:00 am, and more than 100,000 people greeted the sunrise while singing “Growing Toward the Sun (向阳而生)“!

  • Wang Ye, an online self-media operator who specializes in analyzing the equipment and costs of various concerts, followed and filmed a micro-documentary of the Sunrise Concert.

» Yantai Concert Photo Gallery «

Hong Kong Concert

  • This was Hua’s first personal concert outside mainland China.

  • The concert still took the form of a rock festival, and was held for three consecutive days (May 24-26) at the Central Harbourfront Event Space, facing the Victoria Harbour.

  • After 2021, the Mars Concert was finally able to set off fireworks again.

  • And in the stage design of some songs (“God Tree“, “Bullfight“), Smoke Fog Jets were replaced by flame-throwing effect.

  • Hua sang the full version of “I am What I am“ (not just a section in the Cover Songs Medley) at his personal concert after a long absence. This was considered a tribute to Leslie Cheung at the place where he died.

» Hong Kong Concert Photo Gallery «

Nanchang Concert

  • On July 20-21, Hua Chenyu continued his live tour in Nanchang, the capital city of Jiangxi Province, China.

  • For the first performance of the second half of the year, a new four-sided stage design was unveiled, and a completely different setlist was arranged from the rock theme park-style concerts. It was also the first time that Hua sang all his own songs without singing any cover songs. In order to sing more songs, Hua arranged a rock song medley and a fan favorite song medley.

  • A new song will be released in each city in the second half of the year. This time in Nanchang, Hua debuted his new song “Ship of Theseus (忒修斯的船)“.

  • As the weather was extremely hot, a full range of cooling measures were taken. The outdoor air-conditioning fans that were urgently purchased at the Wuhan Concert last year were not used in Changsha due to the rain, but this time they finally came in handy again, spraying cold water mist on the arena all the time before the show started. At the entrance to each block of stand seats, ice buckets were placed to wipe and cool the body. In addition, cooling pads, cooling wipes and menthol balm were distributed free of charge to all audience members.

  • Hua almost got heatstroke while singing on the first day, so in the second half of Day2, he appeared on stage wearing a ice vest that he had worn during rehearsal.

» Nanchang Concert Photo Gallery «

Hefei Concert

  • On August 10-11, Hua Chenyu continued his live tour in Hefei, the capital city of Anhui Province, China.

  • A new song will be released in each city in the second half of the year. This time, Hua debuted his new song “Bizarre Psychology AKA Quirky Psychology (怪诞心理学)“.

  • August 10 is the “Qixi Festival”, which is the Chinese Valentine’s Day based on the romantic legend of the Zhinü and Niulang. As a surprise, Hua gifted each audience with a pack of flower seeds. In addition, the pop-up store sold limited-time snacks (pink soft drinks, red butterfly pastry sets, and flower tea sets).

  • During “Sea of Wind“ on August 10, the big screen showed the most affectionate conversation that Hua and his fans have had in years. From the handwriting, fans inferred that the words shown on the big screen were written by Hua himself.

  • On the 11, while singing the last few sentences of “I’m Here AKA
    I Really Want to
    Love This World    “, Hua squatted down and appeared to be unwell. After the concert, He posted on Weibo: “I’m fine, don’t worry, see you in Chongqing! (我没事，放心吧，我们重庆见！)”




» Hefei Concert Photo Gallery «

Chongqing Concert

  • On August 24, Hua Chenyu continued his live tour in Chongqing city.

  • On that day, the temperature in Chongqing reached 42 degrees Celsius. In addition to cooling pads and cooling wipes, Huoxiang Zhengqi Shui (a traditional Chinese medicine drink for treating heatstroke) and drinking water were also provided free of charge.

  • A new song will be released in each city in the second half of the year. This time, Hua debuted his new song “Warm House (温暖的房子)“.

» Chongqing Concert Photo Gallery «

Beijing (Bird’s Nest) Concert

  • On September 7-8, Hua Chenyu performed at the National Stadium (Bird’s Nest) for the third time.

  • September 8 marks the sixth anniversary of Hua’s first personal concert at the Bird’s Nest. As a commemoration, Hua Chenyu sent physical gifts by courier to all the audience members who purchased tickets through official channels. The gifts include perfumes, scented candles, sachets, hand creams and a variety of T-shirts. The gifts were designed by artist Song Santu and were also exhibited as part of an installation art piece at Mars Concert 2023.

  • At the end of the set list, “Growing Toward the Sun - Sunrise Ver.“ was sung, recreating the grand occasion of the Sunrise Concert.

  • A new song will be released in each city in the second half of the year. This time, Hua debuted his new song Never Cross Paths (不重逢)“.

  • Wang Ye filmed his second micro-documentary for Mars Concert.

» Beijing (Bird's Nest) Concert Photo Gallery «

Guiyang Concert

  • On October 4-6, Hua Chenyu held his last rock festival-style concert of this year for three consecutive days in Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, southwest China.

  • Fireworks were allowed at the venue, and not only were fireworks set off during the last song, but also during the song “Eternal Flame“, several sophisticated rocket-shaped fireworks were set off.

  • At the Matinee, high-pressure fountain mist containing perfume was sprayed on the audience.

  • Guiyang is located in a hilly area with an average altitude of more than 1,000 meters. In autumn, the temperature drops, and Hua feels discomfort in his throat due to the rapid inhalation of a large amount of air when singing. So, he changed his habit of rarely drinking water during performances and began to drink hot water frequently on stage.

  • At the Matinee on the third day, Hua impromptu pulled his friend Ning Huanyu, whom he met on his debut show “Superboy 2013“, from the audience to the stage, and together with Zuo Li, the three of them sang “Follow Me“, a collaborative song composed by Ning.


» Guiyang Concert Photo Gallery «

Hangzhou (Big Lotus) Concert

  • On August 24, Hua Chenyu continued his live tour in Hangzhou. Hangzhou’s newly built “Big Lotus” Stadium is second only to Beijing’s Bird’s Nest in terms of area. The audience for this concert exceeded 80,000 people.

  • A new song will be released in each city in the second half of the year. This time, Hua debuted his new song “Human’s Love (人之爱)“.

  • Taking the stage with a long-lost short hairstyle

  • On the evening before the concert, Hua live-streamed himself touring the stadium. It was the first time for him to personally watch the stage effects from the various levels of the stands, and he said it was much more beautiful and spectacular than what he could see on the stage.

  • During the concert, Hua recalled the Hangzhou stop of the “Superboy 2013“ live tour which he took part in shortly after his debut, and impromptu sang a few lines of “Mr. Almost (差不多先生)”, which he sang back then.

» Hangzhou Concert Photo Gallery «

Wuhan Concert

  • On November 10, Hua Chenyu continued his live tour in his hometown of Wuhan.

  • The opening song was changed to “You Have To Believe This Is Not the Last Day (你要相信这不是最后一天)“, a charity song Hua wrote to support the citizens of Wuhan who have been severely hurt by COVID 19.

  • Wuhan is known as the “Breakfast Capital” of China because of the variety of breakfast options available, and eating breakfast is called “passing breakfast (过早)” in local dialect. On November 7, Hua rode a shared bike alone early in the morning, had breakfast (hot dry noodles, bean curd skin, eggnog), and broadcast the whole thing live on his mobile phone.

  • The day after the concert, Hua Chenyu strolled to the popular check-in spot on Mars where a large number of fans gathered - Wuhan Conservatory of Music (Hua’s alma mater), and lined up with fans to buy the dessert that became popular because of his own favorite.

» Wuhan Concert Photo Gallery «

Shenzhen Concert

  • On November 29-30, Hua Chenyu held the final concert of this year’s tour in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

  • The Mars Concert 2019 held in Haikou was originally scheduled to be held in Shenzhen, and tickets were already sold out, but it was canceled due to force majeure. This year, Hua Chenyu finally fulfilled the promise he made to Shenzhen five years ago.

  • For the promotional poster, Hua also chose to use the 2019 version.

  • A new song will be released in each city in the second half of the year. This time, Hua debuted the last new song “In the Morning Light, There’s You (晨光里有你)“. The word “晨光” in the song title means “morning light” and includes the same Chinese character as “晨” in Hua Chenyu’s name, so the song title can also be interpreted as “Hua Chenyu, in the light, there’s you.”

  • The design of the Rock Theme Park-Style concerts (Guiyang Concert) was transplanted to the stadium, achieving rocket-shaped fireworks and high-pressure fountain mist spraying.

  • On the night before the concert, Hua held a live broadcast on SNS with the theme of “Mars Year-End Party”. Wearing a black suit, Hua imitated the style of a company boss while summarizing this year’s live tour and sharing many anecdotes related to the concerts.

entry.title: Human's Love (人之爱)
entry.content:
First released in “Mars Concert 2024“ Hangzhou concert, on October 26, 2024, and is included in Hua Chenyu’s 6th album “Quantitative Change Tipping Point“.

During the introduction to the song, Hua spent nearly 20 minutes dissecting the concept and the types of love.

Actually, in the past I would usually take a moment at this part to chat with everyone But today I’ve prepared a song for everyone. One that I haven’t sung or released before. So, I’d like to take some time to introduce this song. Alright. Let’s take ten minutes. Since this song has never been performed. And none of you have heard it before. After all, I’m a songwriter. So, I think maybe before singing, I could share the background of creating this work I hope everyone will allow me to be a bit self-indulgent. Alright. Take your time, we want to listen. Lately, for quite a long while I’ve been reflecting on love I wanted to consider human love from a third-person perspective. Why do people come together because of love? And, in the process of being together, face conflicts. And even develop thoughts of wanting to separate.
Later, I realized that most people seem to fall into two types: One is highly sensitive people. The other is less sensitive people. So, what are these two types like? I’ll tell a little story. Let’s make a hypothesis. Suppose today, I’m with a few friends. We’re sitting at a table playing cards. Or playing board games. A few people are playing board games together. At this table, maybe. Most are highly sensitive people. And only one person is less sensitive. So if we’re playing games till around 5 PM and one of the highly sensitive people starts to feel hungry. He might think for a moment and then ask everyone, “About how much longer will we be playing?” At this point, the other highly sensitive people at the table instantly understand and they all subtly glance at the time without saying anything aloud. Maybe some of them aren’t that hungry or are just really enjoying the game at the moment. Then someone might say, “Hey, why don’t we play a couple more rounds and then go eat together—sound good?” At this point, the person who’s hungry might think about it and feel that playing a bit longer, maybe another hour or so, is manageable. So he holds off and waits to eat with everyone. Listening to this some of you might think, “Isn’t that a bit silly? If you’re hungry, just go eat.
Why worry so much about everyone else’s feelings?” But actually, I think this type of person isn’t really compromising himself I believe he made a choice and he’s happy with it. When he decides to play a bit longer with everyone and then go eat together. He feels joy in making a decision that makes everyone else happy. He’s happy inside and not forcing himself. Now, if we imagine a low-sensitivity person starts feeling hungry, they might turn to the person closest to them and ask, “Are we eating? I’m hungry.” When this person says that, you know, everyone at the table might start to feel a sort of… how should I put it… an invisible pressure from not knowing how to respond. There’s a difference between these two questions. The highly sensitive person I mentioned earlier phrased it as, “About how much longer will we be playing?” While the other person said, “Are we eating? I’m hungry.” Why does this create pressure? It’s because no one knows how to respond. If someone replies, “Uh… maybe we should stop playing and go eat,” it feels like everyone hasn’t fully enjoyed the game. But if they say, “Maybe we should eat a bit later,” “We can play a little longer,” there’s a worry that this response might hurt the person. If at this point, their closest friend, someone who’s very familiar with them, responds by saying, “How about we play a bit longer and then eat?” The low-sensitivity person might reply, “No worries, you all keep playing. I’ll just order food for myself.”
I don’t know if everyone understands that feeling. When he says this, the energy in the whole space is disrupted. Those who keep playing may no longer enjoy themselves, and the one who stops playing isn’t happy either. This creates a certain pressure. So, does the low-sensitivity person do anything wrong? I think he’s done nothing wrong at all. He’s just hungry, and he just wants to eat, right? If he’s hungry, he orders food for himself. There’s nothing wrong with that at all. I think he’s pretty cool. Imagine having someone like this in your life—wouldn’t that be cool? Later, I started to ponder the difference between these two types of people.
Then I thought, it seems like this can be divided into three steps. The first step is, when you meet someone, for the first time, your first step might be to observe them. Then, study them. Observe and study at the same time. What does that mean? It means you try to sense what kind of personality this person has, by observing them. Then you observe whether they are an extrovert (E) or an introvert (I). Are they knowledgeable, or not very educated? Are they wealthy or from an average family background? You would study them. Yes, first observe them. Then study them. What I mean is, you study them to get a sense of the kind of environment they grew up in. OK, that’s the first step. Now, the second step, is to anticipate them. By “anticipate,” I mean after you’ve observed and analyzed, you start to think about the potential relationship between you and this person. What might the future connection look like? Can this person be part of your social circle in the future? Could they become your friend? You think, “Hey, this person seems to have a nice personality.” Maybe we could be friends. We get along well. Or, going further, you find this person very attractive. You really like them. So you start to anticipate. You wonder if one day this person might become your lover. You feel like their personality might match well with yours. Anticipation. The third step is to play a role. By “play a role,” I mean for example, when you go out with a friend, and this friend might be feeling down, wanting you to join them for a drink. At that moment, they might be experiencing an 80% emo state, while your emo feeling is only at 8%. But because you want to resonate with them, to connect, you will amplify your own 8% feeling to match their 80%, so you can share the experience. At this point, you two can communicate.
I think most people in life are playing roles. In daily life, we play roles in front of friends, at school, we play the role of a good student, a good friend, a good sister, or a good brother. And in front of the boss at work, we also have to play a role. We are always playing roles. However, such people are very kind. They don’t want to hurt anyone. And I feel that, when I suddenly thought of this, there does seem to be a distinction. Low-sensitivity individuals might only be able to do the first step. Those who are a bit better can do the second step. And high-sensitivity individuals can reach the third step. This creates three types of relationships. For example, if two high-sensitivity people are together, I think they might find it easier to resonate with each other due to constantly playing roles. This might lead to a lot of shared topics. They can easily find many commonalities.
However, the ability to play a role has its limits. That’s why your friends can spend a long time with you. It’s because the time you see your friends each day isn’t very long. So when you finish seeing them, after playing your role for a day, you can be yourself once you leave. But love is different. In love, when two people are living together, after you’ve played your role outside, you still have to play the role of a good wife or a good husband at home, a good partner.
But everyone eventually gets tired. So have you noticed that some people never argue in the first few months of dating? In the beginning, they might not fight at all. They feel the other person has many flaws, but they seem to accept them. But after a few months, those flaws suddenly become problems. Then arguments start to occur. Why is that? Because the time for playing roles has expired. When you decide to start being yourself, that’s when the arguments begin. So I think if two highly sensitive people are together, it should be somewhat better. Their arguments might end more quickly. They might argue and then realize that because of one issue, they’re not really on the same wavelength at that moment. So they might just say, “Forget it! Let’s not argue.” Just imagine that scene: the two of them might be back-to-back, spending the night apart. Then the next day, after they’ve digested their feelings, they can play their roles again. Suddenly, they might think, “ You know, yesterday’s argument wasn’t such a big deal.” Then they reconcile without much effort. This is what we call a cold war. But it resolves quickly.
What if a highly sensitive person is with a low-sensitivity person? I think when these two people are together, the duration of their arguments might be quite long. Especially if both have some knowledge and logical reasoning, a bit of intellect, the argument could extend significantly. Why is that? Because what you say is correct, and what I say is also correct. However, the points we are discussing always remain on parallel lines. Until one side gets tired of arguing. So I feel like all emotional bonds if you think about them hard enough, will inevitably have some pessimistic undertones. Then I wonder, why are there still people who can stay together for so long? I believe that it should be a sense of responsibility.
I think responsibility is a kind of awareness. While love is a kind of perception. So what I want to say is, if you are still single right now, when you choose your partner in the future, I hope or bless you to find a true soul mate. Because this way, you can be more at ease in the future. Even when making choices, your perception can easily overcome your awareness. And… oh, wait, I misspoke. Your awareness can easily overcome your perception. Then you will happily be together for a lifetime, even if there are occasional small arguments.
So if you are already in a relationship or married, maybe some people have already come to terms with it. What about those who are still struggling? I think you need to make a choice. Is perception more important, or is cognition more important? Once you make that choice, you will stop the internal conflict. You will feel much more at ease. Even if you occasionally argue, you will think, “Ah, he is just that kind of person.” I accept that he is just that kind of person. Then you will find life much easier. Similarly, even if you ultimately choose your perception, feeling that you cannot be with this person and decide to break up, that is also a choice you’ve made. You also know that you shouldn’t be too sad or heartbroken. Pain will exist, but I think it doesn’t have to be so devastating. Because this is a choice you made for yourself. You recognize the outcome for both of you, and you anticipate that it would lead to this outcome.
Of course, I’m speaking from the perspective of someone in my thirties, trying to understand love. Right. So I wrote this song. I didn’t write it to be so heart-wrenching. Although I’m good at writing such heart-wrenching songs, I didn’t write it that way. Because I feel that once you understand these things, the so-called pain in movies doesn’t seem so painful. And the warmth isn’t that warm either. Hmm. When writing these lyrics, I also communicated with Lyu Yiqiu (Lyricist) for a long time. We, two men in our thirties, spent two hours on the phone discussing what love is. Then we revised it several times. Sometimes it was too warm, and the second version was too painful. It hurt too much; I didn’t feel it was that painful. So we kept adjusting and adjusting, until we arrived at today’s version of the lyrics.
